mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Extract of the company register for each foreign corporate shareholder (equivalent of a Kbis, Companies House certificate, or Delaware certificate of good standing)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry of the document's country of origin (e.g., UK Companies House, Delaware Division of Corporations, Hong Kong Companies Registry)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the origin state's competent authority for Hague Convention states; Consular Legalization through the French Embassy or Consulate in the origin state for non-Hague states; accompanied by a sworn French translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport/ID copies of all founding shareholders, managers (gérants) and any person empowered to bind the company, together with proof of residential address issued within the last 3 months
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National civil registry, passport authority, or notarial office of the holder's state of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized certified copy (copie certifiée conforme) and, where the document originates outside the European Economic Area, a Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization; sworn translation into French by a translator registered on the list of a French Cour d'appel

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference / AML pedigree letter for each foreign shareholder confirming identity, source of funds, and absence of PEP or sanctions flags
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Overseas credit institution of the shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or direct authenticated bank-to-bank transmission (télétransmission) accepted in practice; French sworn translation required for the RCS file and the French receiving bank

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney (procuration) granted to the French legal representative or law firm for completing incorporation formalities
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Statutory representatives of the foreign corporate shareholder as recorded in its company register
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Signed before a French notary or certified by a notary of the origin state and legalized by Hague Apostille; French sworn translation submitted with the RCS documentation

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against: (1) the EU Commission consolidated financial sanctions list (Reg. (EC) No 2580/2001 and Reg. (EU) No 269/2014); (2) the UN Security Council sanctions lists; (3) the French Treasury asset-freezing orders (arrêtés de gel des avoirs under CMF Article L562-1); (4) the national PEP identification rules of CMF Article L561-10 and R561-18-1 (PEPs, their family members and close associates); and (5) for USD-denominated documentary letters of credit and SWIFT wires, the OFAC SDN list and US correspondent due diligence requirements. Any screening hit on a shareholder, beneficial owner, gérant or counterparty requires an escalated written compliance memo and, where applicable, a Suspicious Transaction Report (STR) to TRACFIN under CMF Article L561-15 before the incorporation file may be advanced.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises operated by INPI (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr), with consultation of the Registre National des Entreprises (RNE), the INPI trademark database, and the territorial Greffe du Tribunal de commerce responsible for the future registered office
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: French is the compulsory drafting language of the corporate name and constitutive documents (Loi n° 94-665 du 4 août 1994, Loi Toubon; Constitution art. 2). The Latin/French alphabet must be used; any foreign element must be transliterated into Latin characters and transliterated copies filed with the Greffe. The corporate name must not mislead the public as to the object of the company, its size, nationality, controlled status, or regulated activity. Foreign-language names are permissible if accompanied by a French equivalent or where not contrary to public policy.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: banque / banker / établissement de crédit (requires prior ACPR authorization)
assurance / assureur / mutuelle (regulated insurance and mutual undertakings)
France / République / national / ministère (creates a false link with public authorities; ministerial authorization required)
avocat / notaire / huissier / expert-comptable / commissaire aux comptes (reserved to regulated professions)
S.A. / S.A.S. / E.U.R.L. / S.A.R.L. when the corporate form does not match
gestion d'actifs / placements / investissement in a securities-marketing context (AMF-sensitive)
commerce, chambre de commerce, ordre (institutional and representative bodies)
sécurité, armée, gendarmerie, douane (state or military implication, requiring prior authorization)
holding (permitted only where the company genuinely holds equity participations)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name may be reserved with INPI for 30 days and renewed once by re-filing and payment of the new €42 fee. If the Guichet unique or the Greffe rejects the reserved name or the subsequent RCS registration on grounds of misleading, unlawful, or confusingly similar nature, the applicant may: (i) submit a corrective refiling through the Guichet unique within 5 working days; (ii) petition the President of the Tribunal de commerce with territorial jurisdiction to order the registrar to register (form 'requête au président du tribunal de commerce' under Article L123-52 of the French Commercial Code) within 8 days of the refusal; and (iii) appeal the President's order to the Cour d'appel within 15 days. A separate INPI trademark opposition procedure (Article L712-4 of the French Intellectual Property Code) is available where refusal is based on an identical earlier trademark.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Authorized under Articles L123-11-2 and L123-11-3 of the French Commercial Code. Professional domiciliation operators holding a prefectoral agreement may host the registered office for up to 6 years; home-domiciliation of a SARL is possible for up to 5 years. However, for the ISIC 2710 heavy electrical equipment activity, a purely virtual office without any operational footprint creates a 'fictive company' (société fictive) risk, may trigger immediate Tax Audit and URSSAF recharacterization, and may prevent the French accepting bank from opening a documentary credit (letter of credit) facility. A physical storage, showroom, or service location is strongly recommended before concluding first high-value export/import contracts and before the RCS registration if the company expects to be treated as having commercial substance in France.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Approximately 12% (+/- 3%) annual probability of an unannounced on-site inspection by URSSAF/DREETS or the Greffe's verification officers for a manufacturing or trading SARL; the likelihood rises to approximately 30% where the registered office is a simple domiciliation box and the company has no French invoicing or payroll within the first six months. French customs (DGDDI) additionally carry out physical inspections of the premises and import records for heavy electrical equipment from non-EU countries, with a higher targeting rate when the supplier or UBO originates from a high-risk foreign jurisdiction.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Company name availability search and reservation with INPI (optional but recommended for a distinctive name and trademark coherence)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI) via the Guichet unique portal
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory INPI tariff: €42 per filing for one main name and one alternative name; no value-added tax applied

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting and legal review of the SARL articles of association (statuts), including shareholder agreements and corporate governance annexes suitable for a single or multiple shareholder structure
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Law firm registered with a French Bar (Avocat au Barreau) or notaire public (notaire)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark: standard SARL statutory package ranges from €1,200 to €1,500 inclusive of VAT in 2024-2025; a notarial act (acte notarié) would add €350-€600 notarial emoluments

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Compulsory legal announcement in a Journal d'Annonces Légales (JAL) authorized by the competent préfecture
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Legal gazette publisher holding the prefectoral authorization (e.g., Affiches Parisiennes, Les Echos, or a regional JAL)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory/regulated line-based rate: average €220-€350 per SARL publication notice, depending on length and chosen gazette (2024 benchmark)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Blocked share capital deposit certificate (attestation de dépôt de fonds) issued by the receiving bank or the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: French credit institution where the capital is temporarily blocked
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Bank schedule: €10-€25 for the issuance of the deposit certificate; 0% interest for the blocking period

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS registration fee (immatriculation au registre du commerce et des sociétés) at the territorially competent Greffe du Tribunal de commerce
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de commerce of the registered office location (e.g., Greffe du Tribunal de commerce de Paris)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff set by the French Ministry of Justice (arrêté du 20 décembre 2022, 2023-2027 pricing): €74.30 for a standard SARL incorporation, inclusive of administrative costs and value added tax

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO (bénéficiaires effectifs) declaration filed as an annex to the RCS registration through the Guichet unique
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Guichet unique operated by INPI on behalf of the Greffe
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No separate statutory filing fee; the declaration forms part of the standard RCS registration dossier. Late or false declarations expose the legal representative to a criminal fine of up to €7,500 and potential imprisonment of 6 months under CMF Article L574-5, so the law firm applies an internal professional check of 0.5-1 hour, included in the statutory drafting fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague Apostille and sworn French translation of foreign corporate documents (3 documents originating from outside France, approx. 5 translation pages)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent authority of the origin state (for apostille) and expert translator registered on the list of a French Cour d'appel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Apostille: fixed statutory fee of the origin state ($10-$25 per document in US jurisdictions, free in certain EU member states); sworn translation: €45-€90 per 250-word page; aggregate estimate of €390 including courier and administrative handling

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) — operational portal www.impots.gouv.fr; company creation via Guichet Unique administered by INPI; VAT registration and administration through the Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE); non-established foreign taxpayers file through Service des Impôts des Entreprises Étrangères (SIEE), Noisy-le-Grand.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate the SARL via the Guichet Unique (INPI) electronic portal, obtaining the SIREN and SIRET registration numbers and automatic notification to the DGFiP tax registry. Step 2: Apply for a French VAT number (numéro de TVA intracommunautaire) by filing Form 4873-SD (Cerfa 15908) with the competent SIE; activation is normally issued with the statutory Kbis attestation. Step 3: For non-established foreign entities, file Form 5078-F (registration of a non-French taxable person) or Form 8474-SD for VAT representative appointment if no permanent establishment and no EU establishment; the SIEE allocates a SIRET with a temporary institutional segment and a French intra-EU VAT number. Step 4: Electronically transmit the VAT registration confirmation to the customs office of economic registration (via POL / DAE) for export privileges. Expected turnaround: 5–10 working days post-incorporation, longer for SIEE file review with apostilled foreign constitutional documents.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election exists in French law. A SARL is mandatorily subject to corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés) at the standard rates, except for a 'SARL de famille' exercising an ‘option for the personal income tax regime’ under Article 239 bis AA CGI, which is available only for eligible close-held family SARLs and is largely incompatible with institutional third-party investors. Options relevant to hybrid instruments: designation of equity versus debt status under Article 239 octies and formal documentation of hybrid branch mismatch arrangements under Article 209 III CGI transposing ATAD; no branch territorial election into a foreign transparent regime unless treated as a French permanent establishment.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée — TVA) harmonized under EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC and codified in Articles 256 to 283 of the French General Tax Code (CGI).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For a French-established SARL in the goods manufacturing sector, VAT registration is obligatory from the first taxable transaction with no de minimis turnover allowance. Deductibility franchise thresholds: €91,000 net annual turnover for goods activities to claim the base exemption (régime de franchise en base) — ineligible for an industrial manufacturer that invoices input VAT. Intra-EU distance sales (B2B/B2C) trigger French registration under the €10,000 European distance-sales threshold under Article 256-0 CGI. Non-established foreign suppliers generating French supply chains: €10,000 annual distance-sales threshold (global EU turnover) for OSS enrollment, and principal place of supply rules for B2B sales to French taxable persons; immediate registration required when the SARL is the importer of record on customs declarations.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory B2B e-invoicing in France phases in under law 2023-1322 (anti-fraud provisions): by 1 September 2026 for large and mid-size enterprises, and by 1 September 2027 for all taxable persons (including SMEs). Invoices must be transmitted using a Dematerialization Partner (PDP) connected to the Public Invoicing Portal (PPF) via the Chorus Pro system. The PPF performs structured data collection, cross-checking, and VAT clearance. API requirements: mandatory use of the Factur-X (hybrid PDF), UBL, or CII syntaxes; structured invoice fields must include VAT identification, B2B customer SIREN/SIRET validation, legal characteristic of the operation, and invoice-level class codes. No physical fiscal stamping applies; instead, the impots.gouv.fr portal and FNFE (Fichier National des Factures Électroniques) repository provide the digital clearance mechanism with real-time transmission obligations and a 72-hour transmission window from invoicing event.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of tangible goods outside the EU are zero-rated under Article 262-I-1° CGI provided that: (i) the goods are physically dispatched or transported outside the European Union by the supplier, on behalf of the supplier, or by a third-party carrier acting on the supplier’s account within the statutory export period; (ii) the SARL is the exporter of record and proof of departure from the EU customs territory is evidenced by the validated electronic Export Declaration (DAE) with the customs IT system (DELTA / POL); (iii) the simultaneous condition of direct transfer of property and actual effect of the sale to the non-EU customer is documented; (iv) payment is received by an authorized FX channel and booked to a registered business bank account in the SARL’s name; (v) the exporter holds the commercial records proving the goods have left the union within 90 days of the release for export (extendable to a reasonable period in justified cases with freight delay customs annex). Export services and related supply of transformer installation services onto third-country sites are zero-rated under Article 262-III-3°C (supplies directly linked to export and associated services closely linked to export, subject to the freight export evidence).
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DAE) — EX-A or EX-A-CO type accepted with the Movement Reference Number (MRN) transmitted by DELTA/POL; customs invoice classified under tariff heading 8504 (and 8537 for switchgear) with correct Schedule B / TARIC nomenclature
Commercial export invoice and packing list (in English) showing Incoterms, unit prices, total invoice value, and ISIC 2710 product description as solid-state power transformer

Bill of Lading (B/L) or Air Waybill (AWB) evidencing loading and arrival at non-EU port of discharge for maritime shipments; CMR consignment note for exemption from VAT on subsequent transport and insurance services (Article 262-III-3°C)
Evidence of payment and FX repatriation: SWIFT MT103 / documentary letter of credit negotiation advice demonstrating receipt of proceeds in the SARL’s French bank account
Customs broker declaration and proof of exporter status (registered EORI number with the French customs authority)
Certificate of origin (optional but recommended to substantiate tariff preference claims under FTAs and bank-requested documents pursuant to LC terms)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating claims are audited against the DEM-application within the EU VAT refund window and the 3-year customs time-bar (Articles 73–84 Union Customs Code). False export declarations or failure to prove effective exit trigger: (i) retrospective VAT repayment at the headline rate as at the date of the unduly zero-rated transaction; (ii) impossibility claim of VAT input deduction on the underlying export contracts; (iii) applying the 80% ‘de mauvaise foi’ increase on amounts evaded under Article 1729-b CGI and 10% late-payment interest under Article 1727 CGI (0.20% per month cap 10%); (iv) penal surcharge of 40% if lack of declaration; (v) criminal prosecution for fiscal fraud under Articles 1741–1743 CGI — up to €500,000 fine and 5 years’ imprisonment for sophisticated export dummy destination schemes; additionally, revocation of the exporter’s EORI license and 100% denial of export privilege on subsequent transactions, plus joint financial liability of the customs representative (déclavant en compte d’autrui) if complicit. Mandatory annual EURESIA Tax Audit Certificate is required where exported turnover exceeds EUR 33 million under the corporate income tax audit framework.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France), acting with the Direction Générale du Trésor (French Treasury) on exchange control, balance-of-payments statistics, and prudential compliance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France is a full Eurozone convertibility jurisdiction. Legal tender is the euro and the capital account is fully liberalised under EU TFEU Articles 63–66, with no French exchange-control permit for lawful cross-border investment by or into a French SARL. Current-account items such as dividends, royalties, commissions, interest and technical service fees are remittable without prior administrative approval, provided corporate tax residence documentation, transfer pricing documentation, and anti-money-laundering source-of-wealth checks are completed. The only operational obstacle is banking KYC, the beneficial-ownership register, and the balance-of-payments reporting requirement: every French resident cross-border flow at or above EUR 50,000 must be identified by the appointed bank under an agreed Banque de France BOP classification code. Profit remittances require distributable reserves verified by the statutory auditor or certified accounts; withholding tax on French dividends (25% standard rate) is reduced by applicable double-taxation treaties and the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory obligation to surrender export proceeds or to convert foreign currency into euro, because France has no exchange surrender or compulsory conversion regime. Export receipts may be retained in USD, CNY or other freely convertible currencies in an account held in France or in another EU/EEA jurisdiction, subject to French balance-of-payments reporting. If the cross-border trade-in-goods payment is below EUR 50,000, no special declaration is required. At or above EUR 50,000, the settlement bank assigns the BOP economic code for merchandise exports, and the remitter must provide a commercial invoice, transport documentation, and the customs export declaration (SAD/ENS). Where the payment resides in a non-euro currency, the SARL may request conversion to EUR at the bank's intraday rate; no surrender law applies. The SARL should include in each SWIFT instruction a clear reference such as 'export of solid-state transformer equipment under ISIC 2710' to expedite BOP classification.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole Group (Crédit Agricole CIB / local Caisse régionale)
BPCE Group (Banque Populaire and Caisse d'Épargne)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: MEDIUM for operational treasury, LOW for documentary trade finance. A fintech e-money institution licensed by the ACPR under the French Monetary and Financial Code or passported from another EU authority can provide multi-currency IBANs, payment accounts, SEPA and SWIFT wire disbursement for routine supplier payments. However, an EMI cannot issue or confirm documentary letters of credit, accept term deposits, extend real credit lines, or execute derivative FX hedging, because it is not a credit institution. For high-value solid-state transformer export/import settlements, LC issuance and complex liquidity management, a fully licensed French commercial bank remains mandatory.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is not a statutory absolute for a French SARL. Qualitative remote onboarding is generally feasible using a videoconference interview and an eIDAS-qualified electronic signature or validated French identity verification. In practice, major French banks accept remote opening for a low-risk manufacturing/distribution SARL if the legal representative and all beneficial owners provide reliable passports, French proof of address, updated KBis, the UBO declaration and notarised powers if authority is delegated. The bank may still require a physical or notarised meeting for non-resident directors, complex ownership, a sanction-sensitive transaction geography, or where screening raises difficulty. Remote onboarding at BNP Paribas and Société Générale normally completes within two to four weeks once the corporate document package is complete.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Invoice counterparty is a recently incorporated offshore shell purchaser with no verifiable industrial substance in the electrical equipment sector.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: The file must include the French KBis of the SARL, UBO declaration, the counterparty's corporate extract and shareholders' register, audited annual accounts or unaudited statutory accounts, tax numbers, bank references, signed sale contract, commercial pro forma invoice, Incoterms certificate, packing list, bill of lading / CMR / AWB referencing the transformer equipment, customs SAD export declaration, EORI numbers of both parties and a corporate-organisation chart demonstrating the real end-customer relationship.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholders injecting paid-in capital through a high-risk third-country jurisdiction listed on the FATF grey list or the French tax non-cooperative state list.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: The bank will require each shareholder's identity document (passport or national ID), proof of registration in the home jurisdiction, good-standing certificate apostilled or legalised, certified copy of the source of wealth (commercial contracts, bank statements, tax returns, or sale of goods documents), a reference from a reputable upstream bank, UBO declaration, source-of-funds proof immediately before transfer, notarised capital subscription deed, SARL board minute approving the capital increase, and an explanatory affidavit connecting the capital transfer to the transformer equipment manufacturing project.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: SWIFT payment purpose does not match the declared ISIC 2710 business because the instruction references a generic code or vague commercial narrative.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a treasury instruction note referencing the signed purchase order, the exact ISIC/NACE code, the export/import contract in the relevant language, the commercial invoice with a detailed equipment description, the HS classification and ECCN if dual-use controls apply, customs SAD/ENS documentation, transport waybill, packing list, insurance certificate, and the bank's BOP code for merchandise trade. The SARL should maintain an evergreen counterparty onboarding pack allowing the bank to re-screen swiftly.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity or shareholder-loan capital must be wired to the French SARL's dedicated capital escrow or operational account using a French IBAN (FR76 + BIC) and SWIFT MT103 for non-SEPA transfers. The payment instruction must state the Banque de France BOP direct-investment category and the explicit purpose phrase: 'APPORT EN COMPTE COURANT D'ASSOCIE' for shareholder loans or 'APPORT DE CAPITAL SOCIAL' for equity. The bank will require the updated KBis, dated contribution deed, shareholder resolution, UBO declaration, proof of source of funds, and confirmation of the bank's conversion rate if the remittance is in a currency other than euro. Funds may only be deployed after the capital increase has been registered and a creditor notice period under French law, if applicable, is fulfilled.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound supplier payments in the EU are cleared through SEPA Credit Transfer with the beneficiary's IBAN. Non-EU supplier payments, local freight, spare parts and warranty disbursements use the SWIFT MT103 with the correct BOP trade code and the counterparty bank BIC. For large-scale transformer component purchases, the primary clearing rail is an irrevocable documentary Letter of Credit issued by the French bank via SWIFT MT700 and amended through MT707. The UCP600 and ISBP rules govern document presentation; settlement occurs by the issuing bank paying the nominated bank through SWIFT MT103 on presentation of compliant documents. Standby LC and bank guarantees are issued via SWIFT MT760. All outbound payments must include the invoice/reference number, a clear trade-purpose narrative, and matching transport/customs evidence in the bank's document portal.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable FX forward in EUR/USD, EUR/CNY and other convertible currencies for firm import/export commitments
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for sanctioned or restricted EEMEA/Asia cross-border currencies where a deliverable forward is unavailable
Deliverable cross-currency swaps for long-term USD/EUR working capital and receivables matching
Vanilla FX options (purchased) as risk-reversal hedging for competitive tender exposures without speculative options
FX embedded in commodity-independent commercial freight invoicing and special-purpose treasury swaps under EMIR clearing requirements

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (RCS France)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 6 months after financial year-end (e.g. 30 June for calendar year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to €10,000; company dissolution risk after 3 months of non-compliance notice

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Update of Beneficial Owners Declaration (Déclaration des Bénéficiaires Effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (RCS France)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days of any ownership or control change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to €10,000; potential sanctions for non-compliance

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory statutory audit if company exceeds two of: turnover > €50 million, balance sheet total > €43 million, or average employees > 500

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annual review and update of UBO information in RCS if changes occurred; maintain declaration current

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% standard rate from fiscal year 2022 onward; reduced 15% rate applies to the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit for a qualifying small-and-medium enterprise with annual turnover not exceeding EUR 10,000,000 (CGI art. 219 I).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% rate on the first EUR 42,500 of profit; Research Tax Credit (Crédit d'Impôt Recherche) at 30% of eligible R&D expenditure up to EUR 100,000,000 per year and 5% above that cap; Innovation Tax Credit (Crédit d'Impôt Innovation) at 20% of qualifying novel-product development up to EUR 400,000 per year; accelerated depreciation for energy-efficient transformers and heavy electrical equipment; social solidarity contribution (contribution sociale de solidarité) at 0.125% of turnover above EUR 760,000.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited carryforward under art. 209 CGI, but each year's offset is capped at EUR 1,000,000 plus 50% of the taxable profit exceeding EUR 1,000,000; no separate carry-back for losses generated after fiscal year 2021.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD (déclaration de résultat) together with the 2050-series schedules (balance sheet, income statement) and annexes 2058-A/2059-A for fiscal adjustments and loss carryforward; mandatory electronic filing via the EFI module of impots.gouv.fr in the professional taxpayer space ('Votre espace professionnel') under the SARL's SIREN/SIRET.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual return; quarterly instalments (acomptes) of corporate income tax due on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September and 15 December; final balance ('solde') paid with the annual return via the RBS (relevé de solde).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a fiscal year closing on 31 December, the statutory filing deadline is the second working day following 1 May of the next year (illustration: FY 2024 returns due 5 May 2025); for a closing date other than 31 December, the return must be filed within three months of the closing date; non-electronic filing triggers a EUR 15,000 fine.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, legal form (SARL), share capital, SIREN/SIRET number, APE/NAF code 2710Z, address of registered office and date of incorporation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert the French registrations as issued by INSEE; the non-resident shareholders are not disclosed here; the French gérant (manager) must appear as the legal representative and signatory.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Principal activity description: manufacture of high-voltage power transformers and switchgear (ISIC 2710 / NAICS 335311); indication that the activity is an industrial manufacturing operation in France.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Keep the description aligned with the registered Activity (APE) code; any secondary trading or distribution activity must be separately disclosed to avoid TP recharacterization.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net accounting profit or loss of the French statutory accounts before tax (bénéfice or déficit comptable), prepared under French GAAP (PCG).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Amounts must be in EUR and reconciled to the approved financial statements; transfer pricing adjustments already booked in the statutory accounts are reported here at gross value.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-deductible expenses to be added back: fines, penalties, excessive directors' fees, non-deductible taxes, non-arm's-length payments, 5% reattribution of dividends from EU subsidiaries, and payments to non-cooperative jurisdictions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reintégrations must be supported by an internal memo; a non-resident parent must not direct the French manager to omit TP add-backs.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible items not recorded in the statutory accounts: dividend-received exemption (95% under art. 216 CGI), certain provisions, export subsidies and tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach the investment holding evidence and the 2-year holding commitment if the SARL benefits from the parent-subsidiary regime; foreign tax credits must be documented with TRC.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal result before loss carryforward, computed as accounting result plus réintégrations less déductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Verify that intercompany purchases of transformer components from foreign affiliates are booked at arm's length; the fiscal result is the starting point for any transfer pricing audit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prior-year tax losses offset against the fiscal result of the current year, subject to the EUR 1,000,000 plus 50% excess cap of art. 209 CGI.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A schedule of loss history must be retained; the cap must be computed on the fiscal result before carryforward; losses of foreign permanent establishments cannot be imputed unless the PE is taxed in France.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable base for the corporate income tax (base imposable) to which the 15% reduced rate (first EUR 42,500 for eligible SMEs) and 25% standard rate are applied.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The non-resident parent should ensure the French entity's taxable base is determined under art. 57 CGI with full comparability evidence; no allocation of group headquarters costs without an appropriate service agreement.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income tax credits and reductions: research tax credit (CIR), innovation tax credit (CII), foreign tax credit for taxes paid abroad on French-source taxable items.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Supporting forms 2069-A (CIR) and 2069-B (CII) must be filed; foreign tax credits require a TRC and no double-deduction of the same foreign tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: 2065-RBS (Relevé de solde de l'impôt sur les sociétés)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of the final IS balance: tax due at 15%/25%, less quarterly instalments paid, leaving the amount payable on the filing date.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Instalment payments are computed on the previous fiscal year's taxable result; a non-resident parent cannot offset group tax balances against the French SARL's instalments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Social solidarity contribution of 0.125% assessed on turnover (excluding VAT) exceeding EUR 760,000; an additional 0.125% applies when turnover exceeds EUR 3,000,000,000.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The base is French turnover only, excluding exports invoiced through a foreign group company; sales routed to the French entity by a non-resident trader do not enter the CSS base.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Country-by-Country Report notification form filed when the French SARL belongs to a group with consolidated revenue of at least EUR 750,000,000, disclosing the reporting entity.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the group qualifies, the SARL must file the notification even if the ultimate parent is foreign; failure to file triggers a penalty and the denial of the absence-of-file defense.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing without formal notice: 10% surcharge on the tax due; within 30 days of a formal notice: 40%; after 30 days or in case of concealed activity: 80%; plus late-payment interest of 0.20% per month (2.4% per annum) under art. 1727 CGI; EUR 15,000 fine for non-electronic filing (art. 1731 BA CGI); EUR 15,000 fine for missing transfer pricing documentation file (art. 1731 ter CGI); assessment d'office (taxation d'office) may be imposed under art. L.66 LPF.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 30% on gross dividends paid to non-resident corporate shareholders in the absence of treaty or EU protection (CGI arts. 119 bis and 187); 0% for EU/EEA corporate shareholders qualifying under the Parent–Subsidiary Directive (arts. 145 and 216 CGI, direct 10% or 25% holding maintained for two years, 95% exemption with 5% reattribution); typical treaty rates: 15% general United States rate, 5% where the US parent owns at least 10% of voting power, 15% general United Kingdom rate, 0% for UK companies controlling at least 25% of the paying company under substance conditions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The French SARL (as payer) may apply the reduced rate at source upon receiving, before payment, a duly executed attestation de résidence fiscale (forms 5000/5001/5002 series or OECD-specified TRC) signed by the foreign tax authority in the year of payment, together with a beneficial-ownership statement and, for EU parents, the form 5030/5031 commitment regarding the two-year holding condition. The documentation is lodged with the Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE) at the SARL's registered office. If the dividend has already suffered 30% French withholding, the foreign shareholder must file a refund claim (réclamation contentieuse) before 31 December of the second year following the year of collection under art. R.196-1 LPF.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties for patents and industrial property: statutory withholding of 33.33% (CGI art. 182 B bis); royalties for copyrights and software licences: 20%. EU Interest & Royalties Directive (transposed in art. 131 quater CGI) suppresses the withholding entirely where royalties or interest are paid to an associated EU company holding 25% directly for at least two years. Arm's-length interest paid to non-resident corporate lenders is generally exempt from French withholding (CGI art. 125 A III); payments to shareholders that are recharacterized as disguised dividends attract the 30% dividend withholding, and interest paid to beneficiaries in non-cooperative jurisdictions attracts a 75% withholding under art. 125 A III.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Full mandatory documentation (local file, master file and country-by-country report) applies where (i) the French entity's annual turnover or gross balance-sheet assets equal or exceed EUR 400,000,000, or (ii) the French entity is owned, directly or indirectly, more than 50% by a group entity meeting that threshold (art. L.13 AA LPF; BOI-BIC-BASE-40-10-40). Country-by-Country Reporting is mandatory where the consolidated group revenue reaches EUR 750,000,000, with local submission of form 2258-SD. For a manufacturing SARL below these thresholds, contemporaneous light documentation (intercompany agreements, benchmarks for the sale of transformers to related distributors, margin analysis at 8-12% cost-plus or TNMM) must nevertheless be maintained for audit defense.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France is not an Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) jurisdiction in the offshore sense, but applies equivalent substance doctrines: siège de direction effective (art. 8 CGI) for tax residence; the abuse-of-law procedure (abus de droit, art. L.64 LPF); the general anti-abuse rule for treaty benefits (art. 205A CGI); the beneficial-ownership requirement of the OECD Model and EU Directives; and the anti-artificial-arrangement rule of the Parent–Subsidiary Directive (art. 119 ter CGI). A French SARL manufacturing high-voltage transformers and switchgear from a real French plant with employed industrial staff, inventory and Capex maintains valid economic substance; a letterbox SARL without personnel or premises will be treated as an artificial entity, denied treaty benefits, and reassessed at the 30% domestic withholding on all distributions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentional concealment of transformer sales revenue, under-invoicing related-party sales, issuance of fictitious export invoices, off-the-books cash receipts, manipulation of documentary letters of credit to divert proceeds from the French entity, or false statements in the 2065-SD return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil: reassessment d'office of the concealed profit, penalty of 40% for bad faith or 80% for fraudulent manoeuvres (arts. 1729 and 1732 CGI), and 0.20% per-month late-payment interest; the 3-year reopening period is extended to 6 years in cases of abuse. Criminal: up to 5 years' imprisonment and EUR 75,000 fine under art. 1741 CGI; aggravated fraud (organized gang) carries 7 years and EUR 100,000; the court may order confiscation, publication of judgment, and deprivation of civic, civil and family rights.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The gérant may be declared personally liable for the company's tax debt and penalties when the administrative court finds manœuvres frauduleuses or inobservation grave et répétée des obligations fiscales (art. L.267 LPF); a criminal conviction may impose travel bans (interdiction de quitter le territoire), prohibition on managing a business (faillite personnelle), freezing of personal assets, and joint civil restitution of the amounts evaded.
